messages.subject: multigroup analysis on regression estimates
parts:
Hi there, 

I just performed a measurement invariance between two groups in my dataset. My invariance is strong, which means I can compare both groups without any problems. But I was wondering if it's possible now to compare the regressions of both models? Can I conclude there is a significant difference between the standardized regression estimates? And which "code" in Lavaan can I use to obtain this information? 

Could it be that the function measurementInvariance() does not work anymore?
I had to do it this way:

 #Model1: configural invariance
> fit1 <-sem(model=Model18, data=mydata, estimator="ML", group="V4")
> 
> #Model2: weak invariance
> fit2 <-sem(model=Model18, data=mydata, estimator="MLR", group="V4", 
+            group.equal="loadings")
> 
> #Model3: strong invariance
> fit3 <-sem(model=Model18, data=mydata, estimator="MLR", group="V4", 
+            group.equal=c("loadings", "intercepts"))
> anova(fit1, fit2)
Chi Square Difference Test

      Df   AIC   BIC  Chisq Chisq diff Df diff Pr(>Chisq)
fit1 272 26002 26612 362.80                              
fit2 284 25995 26555 379.62     16.821      12     0.1565
> anova(fit1, fit3)
Chi Square Difference Test

      Df   AIC   BIC  Chisq Chisq diff Df diff Pr(>Chisq)
fit1 272 26002 26612 362.80                              
fit3 296 25977 26487 385.66     22.855      24     0.5284
> anova(fit2, fit3)
Scaled Chi Square Difference Test (test = yuan.bentler)

      Df   AIC   BIC  Chisq Chisq diff Df diff Pr(>Chisq)
fit2 284 25995 26555 360.56                              
fit3 296 25977 26487 367.30     6.1457      12     0.9086

Thank you for your help!

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: multigroup analysis on regression estimates
parts:
> without any problems. But I was wondering if it's possible now to
> compare the regressions of both models? Can I conclude there is a
> significant difference between the standardized regression estimates?

Hm. That is not trivial. To formally compare unstandardized regression
estimates across groups, you could label them, as in

y ~ c(a1,a2,a3)*x

(where I have assumed there are 3 groups), and then define new
parameters which reflect the difference between two regression coefficients:

diff.a1a2 := a1 - a2
diff.a1a3 := a1 - a3

This would then give you a standard error and a p-value. However, to do
this for standardized regression coefficients, you would need to first
manually compute the standardized regression coefficients. Now, a
standardized beta (z.beta) is simply

z.beta = beta * (sd(x)/sd(y))

You could get the values for the variances of y and x from the diagonal
of inspect(fit, "cov.ov") if they are observed, and inspect(fit,
"cov.lv") if they are latent. Suppose the (fitted) variances for y and x
are 10 and 7 in group 1, then you could write

z.a1 = a1 * sqrt(7)/sqrt(10).

The same for z.a2 and z.a2 (but now using the variances of y and x from
groups 2 and 3). And then, finally, you can write

diff.za1za2 := z.a1 - z.a2
> Could it be that the function measurementInvariance() does not work anymore?
The measurementInvariance() function has moved to the semTools package.

> I had to do it this way:
>
> #Model1: configural invariance
> > fit1 <-sem(model=Model18, data=mydata, estimator="ML", group="V4")
> >
> > #Model2: weak invariance
> > fit2 <-sem(model=Model18, data=mydata, estimator="MLR", group="V4",
> + group.equal="loadings")
> >
> > #Model3: strong invariance
> > fit3 <-sem(model=Model18, data=mydata, estimator="MLR", group="V4",
> + group.equal=c("loadings", "intercepts"))
> > anova(fit1, fit2)

But this is the 'good' way: you see what your are doing.

Yves.
